newsitem.title: FRANCE: French call off search for mystery crash in Alps.
newsitem.headline: French call off search for mystery crash in Alps.

text.p: Rescue teams called off a search for a suspected crashed plane in the hills around this French Alpine village on Thursday, after witness reports of a mysterious fireball over the mountains.

Residents of the village of Dingy-St Clair, between Annecy and Thones in southeastern France and some 50 km (30 miles) from Geneva, told a Reuters television crew they heard a plane noise and an explosion at dawn and saw a light in the sky.
Witnesses reported seeing the fireball over the mountains of Parleman about 10 km (six miles) east of Annecy at around five a.m. (0400 GMT).
Rescue work was hampered by bad weather which later cleared to allow two police helicopters to search the mountaintops.
By mid-afternoon the search had been called off. Local officials said that no accident involving a plane had taken place.
A Russian Antonov-12, an aircraft known to be very noisy, had flown over the area earlier in the day at the time witnesses reported hearing an explosion, officials said.
Air traffic controllers in Aix-en-Provence, who control air traffic over the south of France including international flights, said they had no reports of missing planes.
International flights are tracked on radar and none had disappeared from screens.
The owner of a local restaurant, Remond Dervaison, reported hearing the noise of a plane flying over the village.
Added an elderly village resident, Emma Panittet: "I heard a big bang noise and saw a blue light in the sky."
The village mayor, Monique Zurecki, said: "It probably was a small plane, perhaps a small military plane."
But airports and air traffic controllers in France and neighbouring Italy and Switzerland, baffled by speculation of a crash, said there were no reports of missing planes.

"We have no explanation," said a spokesman for the French aviation authority. He doubted a theory that there had been a secret flight by a small private plane, saying: "To go flying at night in the mountains in a snowstorm would be to take a huge risk."
